# FDG9033

> DO keep parameters in the same order in the synchronous and asynchronous variants of a method, when possible.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.4 Making an Async Variant of an Existing Synchronous Method.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9033
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Keep the parameters of '{0}' in the same order as in the synchronous method '{1}'

FDG9033 reports an externally visible method whose name ends with "Async" and which returns a task-like type (as for FDG9020) when the methods of the same type named without the suffix, its synchronous variants, static or not as it is and not returning a task-like type, that share at least two parameter names with it all have those names in a different relative order. There is no report when one such variant has the same order, since the asynchronous method then aligns with it, and a variant that shares fewer than two names is not compared. CancellationToken parameters are left out, since the asynchronous variant adds its token last (FDG9024), and parameters that only one of the two has are ignored, as the conversions of ref and out parameters (FDG9034) need. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, and variants in other types or with other names are not seen, so coverage is partial. FDG5003 compares the order across overloads. Reordering changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

When the synchronous method has no parameters passed as `out` or `ref`, and neither the return value or any of the parameters are ref-like value types (`ref struct` types), then you can declare the asynchronous variant by just adding the “Async” suffix, changing the return type to the appropriate Task-like type (section 9.2.3), and accepting a `CancellationToken`. For example:

```csharp
public partial class XDocument {
  public static XDocument Load(
    TextReader textReader, LoadOptions options) { ... }

  // The real XDocument.LoadAsync does not have a default value for
  // cancellationToken; this version is better aligned with the
  // guidance in this section.
  public static Task<XDocument> LoadAsync(
    TextReader textReader, LoadOptions options,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
}
```
